sentences.en: But he had forgotten to check the stock first.

sentences.en: By the time I counted the bottles inside, I felt a cold knot in my stomach.
sentences.cn: 等我数完里面的瓶子，我感到肚子里一阵冰冷。

achieve:1.en: Tang had bet the Manager she could sell thirty bags of chips before noon just by standing outside and smiling at passers-by. No words, just a smile. By eleven-fifty she had sold twenty-nine. She stared at the street, willing someone to walk over. To *achieve* thirty felt huge.
achieve:1.cnHint: 唐打赌只靠微笑就能在中午前卖出三十包薯片，还差最后一包。
achieve:1.hook: A dog walker paused, looked at the chips, then looked at Tang.
achieve:1.line: I will *achieve* thirty bags before that clock strikes noon.

sentences.en: Tang had bet the Manager she could sell thirty bags of chips before noon just by standing outside and smiling at passers-by.
sentences.cn: 阿糖跟店长打赌,说她能在中午前就靠站在外面对路人微笑卖出三十袋薯片。

sentences.en: She stared at the street, willing someone to walk over.
sentences.cn: 她盯着街道,希望有人走过来。

challenge:1.en: Lin walked across the street and stopped in front of our sale sign. He crossed his arms and looked at me. 'I *challenge* you,' he said quietly, 'to match my prices.' He slid a handwritten list across the pavement with his shoe. I picked it up. My hands went cold.

challenge:1.hook: Every price on his list was lower than ours by exactly one yuan.
challenge:1.line: I *challenge* you to beat these prices this weekend.

sentences.en: I picked it up.

power:1.en: At midnight the street lights on our corner flickered and went out. The store stayed bright, but outside it was suddenly very dark. A couple who had been reading our window menu stepped back, unsure. 'We still have *power*,' I called out from the doorway. They looked relieved and stepped inside.
power:1.cnHint: 路灯突然灭了，我在门口告诉驻足的顾客，我们店还有____。
power:1.hook: Behind me, somewhere deep in the store, something beeped twice.

sentences.en: At midnight the street lights on our corner flickered and went out.
sentences.cn: 午夜时分,拐角处的路灯闪烁,然后熄灭了。

sentences.en: The store stayed bright, but outside it was suddenly very dark.

sentences.cn: 他们松了口气,走进了店里。

receive:1.en: Saturday morning. A delivery van stops outside the store. The Manager rushes out, clipboard in hand, counting boxes stacked on the pavement. 'Sign here,' the driver says. The Manager checks each label twice. We are about to *receive* forty cases of weekend sale stock, and not a single one matches the order sheet.
receive:1.cnHint: 店长在店门口____了一大批促销货物，却发现数量对不上。
receive:1.hook: One box is ticking softly from inside.
receive:1.line: 'We *receive* forty cases, but the list says thirty-eight.'

sentences.cn: 星期六早上。

sentences.en: A delivery van stops outside the store.

encourage:1.en: Lin stands on the pavement handing out small flyers for a rival shop two streets away. She spots me taping our sale poster to the window and grins. 'Nice try,' she calls. But the Manager appears beside me and gives my shoulder a firm pat. 'Let her watch,' he says, trying to *encourage* me to keep going.

encourage:1.hook: Lin folds one of our flyers and slips it into her pocket.
encourage:1.line: 'I always *encourage* my team before a big sale day.'

sentences.en: 'Let her watch,' he says, trying to *encourage* me to keep going.

travel:1.en: Old Mr. Chen arrives before sunrise, pulling a small cart loaded with homemade rice balls. He says the same thing every Saturday: the best customers *travel* all the way from the new apartments just to buy from our corner. He sets his cart beside our entrance without asking, arranges the balls neatly, and winks at me.
travel:1.cnHint: 陈大爷说顾客们会专程____到我们这个街角来买东西。
travel:1.hook: This Saturday, his cart carries something wrapped in dark cloth.
travel:1.line: 'People *travel* far for good food — remember that, young clerk.'

sentences.en: Chen arrives before sunrise, pulling a small cart loaded with homemade rice balls.

strong:1.en: The weekend wind picks up just as Tang and I finish hanging a long banner across the store front. The banner snaps hard in the gust. Tang tests the rope with both hands and nods. 'The knot is *strong*,' she says. She is right — the banner holds while every other shop's sign along the street tears loose.
strong:1.cnHint: 唐检查了绳结，确认它____，足以撑过大风。
strong:1.hook: Then one corner nail begins to pull slowly from the wall.
strong:1.line: 'Don't worry — this knot is *strong* enough for any storm.'

sentences.en: The weekend wind picks up just as Tang and I finish hanging a long banner across the store front.
sentences.cn: 当阿糖和我刚好把一条长横幅挂在店铺前时,周末的风吹了起来。

sentences.cn: 阿糖用两只手拉了拉绳子,点点头。

sentences.cn: 她说对了——横幅牢牢挂着,而街上其他店铺的招牌都被吹破了。

chance:1.en: A woman in a yellow coat stops at our window display, stares at the stacked tins, then walks away. A minute later she is back. The Manager leans over to me and whispers that this is our *chance* to show her the weekend deal before she crosses the street to Lin's shop. I open the door and smile.
chance:1.cnHint: 店长低声提醒我，现在是抓住这位顾客的____。
chance:1.hook: The woman's yellow coat hides a staff badge from Lin's store.
chance:1.line: 'This is our *chance*, so go and greet her warmly.'

sentences.en: A woman in a yellow coat stops at our window display, stares at the stacked tins, then walks away.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着黄色外套的女人停在咱们的橱窗展示前,盯着堆放的罐子看,然后走开了。

sentences.en: A minute later she is back.
sentences.cn: 一分钟后她回来了。

sentences.en: The Manager leans over to me and whispers that this is our *chance* to show her the weekend deal before she crosses the street to Lin's shop.
I open the door and smile.
sentences.cn: 我打开门,咧嘴一笑。

solve:1.en: Tang discovers a jammed price-tag printer right when the Saturday rush begins. Customers are already queuing at the door. The Manager paces. I borrow a thick marker from the stationery rack and hand-write every price on plain cards. It takes six minutes to *solve* the problem, and the queue does not complain — much.
solve:1.cnHint: 标价打印机坏了，我用记号笔手写价格卡，____了这个问题。
solve:1.hook: But the Manager notices one card has the wrong price on it.
solve:1.line: 'Good — you *solve* small problems before they grow big.'

sentences.en: It takes six minutes to *solve* the problem, and the queue does not complain — much.

quite:1.en: By mid-morning the pavement outside is *quite* crowded. Families with pushchairs, elderly neighbours with bags, and school kids pressing their faces to the glass all squeeze past each other in front of our door. Tang stands just inside, keeping count on a small notebook. She has never seen a Saturday like this in two years of working here.
quite:1.cnHint: 今天上午街边____热闹，唐说这是她两年来没见过的盛况。
quite:1.hook: Tang's notebook count suddenly skips from forty to sixty-three.
quite:1.line: 'It is *quite* busy — stay near the door and guide them in.'

sentences.en: By mid-morning the pavement outside is *quite* crowded.

sentences.en: Tang stands just inside, keeping count on a small notebook.

sentences.cn: 在这儿工作的两年里,她从没见过这样的星期六。

technology:1.en: A teenager outside is using his phone to scan the QR code on our sale poster. He taps the screen, frowns, taps again. 'Your link is broken,' he tells me. I had no idea the Manager had added any *technology* to the promotion at all. I call inside for help, and Tang comes out holding a printed sheet with the correct code.

technology:1.line: 'New *technology* is great — when someone remembers to test it.'

option:1.en: A woman with two heavy bags stops outside and stares at our weekend bundle display. 'Is there any other *option* besides the large pack?' she asks me. 'I live alone. The large size is too much.' She looks tired. I think fast, then point to a sign she has clearly missed.

sentences.cn: 阿糖及时接住了托盘，对我竖了个疲倦的大拇指。

wrong:1.en: Lin stood outside our store, staring at the sale signs I had just put up. Something about Lin's face told me a *wrong* price had slipped through. I checked the tag on the sparkling water — it said two yuan instead of twelve. Lin smiled, said nothing, and walked away. I fixed it fast, my ears turning red.
wrong:1.cnHint: 林盯着我贴的促销价签，我意识到上面有一个____的数字。
wrong:1.hook: Had Lin already photographed the tag?
wrong:1.line: 'That price is *wrong* — you might want to fix it quickly.'

sentences.en: Lin stood outside our store, staring at the sale signs I had just put up.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在我们店外，盯着我刚贴上去的促销牌。

sentences.en: Something about Lin's face told me a *wrong* price had slipped through.
I checked the tag on the sparkling water — it said two yuan instead of twelve.
sentences.cn: 我检查了苏打水的价签——上面写的是两块钱，而不是十二块。

sentences.en: Lin smiled, said nothing, and walked away.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林笑了笑，什么也没说，走开了。

sentences.en: I fixed it fast, my ears turning red.
sentences.cn: 我飞快地改了过来，耳朵烧红了。

variety:1.en: For the weekend sale the Manager told me to group the snacks by type outside the entrance. I was surprised by the *variety* of things we sold — dried fruit, rice crackers, seaweed chips, and even small jars of spicy sauce. A kid stopped, eyes wide, and pointed at nearly everything. Her grandmother just sighed and opened her purse.
variety:1.cnHint: 周末大促时，我把零食分类摆出来，才发现店里售卖的东西____真丰富。
variety:1.hook: The grandmother whispered something to the kid that made them both laugh.
variety:1.line: 'Look at this *variety* — I do not know where to start!'

sentences.en: For the weekend sale the Manager told me to group the snacks by type outside the entrance.
sentences.cn: 周末促销时，店长让我在入口外把零食按类型分组摆放。

sentences.en: I was surprised by the *variety* of things we sold — dried fruit, rice crackers, seaweed chips, and even small jars of spicy sauce.
A kid stopped, eyes wide, and pointed at nearly everything.
sentences.cn: 一个小孩停了下来，睁大眼睛，指向几乎所有的东西。

sentences.en: Her grandmother just sighed and opened her purse.
sentences.cn: 她的奶奶只是叹了口气，打开了钱包。

clear:1.en: I wrote the sale prices on a small whiteboard and set it on the pavement. Tang walked past, squinted, and shook his head. My handwriting was too small. I rubbed it all out and wrote again, big and bold this time. Now it was *clear* enough to read from across the street. An old man nodded at it approvingly and walked straight in.
clear:1.cnHint: 我在小白板上写了促销价，但字太小，重新写了一遍，终于____可以让对面的人看到了。
clear:1.hook: The old man came out holding something we did not even know was on sale.
clear:1.line: 'Much better — now it is *clear* for everyone passing by.'

sentences.en: I wrote the sale prices on a small whiteboard and set it on the pavement.
sentences.cn: 我在一个小白板上写下了促销价格，把它放在人行道上。

sentences.en: Tang walked past, squinted, and shook his head.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林走过时，眯起眼睛，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: My handwriting was too small.
sentences.cn: 我的笔迹太小了。

sentences.en: I rubbed it all out and wrote again, big and bold this time.
sentences.cn: 我把它全擦掉，这次写得又大又粗。

sentences.en: Now it was *clear* enough to read from across the street.
An old man nodded at it approvingly and walked straight in.
sentences.cn: 一个老先生点了点头，直接走了进去。

gain:1.en: By eight in the morning a short queue had formed outside. I watched people fill their baskets quickly, and I started to understand what the weekend sale was really about. Every small purchase was a *gain* for the store, yes, but the real reward was the warm feeling of neighbours choosing us over the bigger shop down the road. Lin peered over from across the street.
gain:1.cnHint: 周末早上门外排起了队，我意识到每一笔小销售都是店里的一份____。
gain:1.hook: Lin was writing something in a small notebook.
gain:1.line: 'Every loyal customer is a *gain* we should never take for granted.'

sentences.en: By eight in the morning a short queue had formed outside.
sentences.cn: 早上八点的时候，外面已经排起了一小队。

sentences.en: I watched people fill their baskets quickly, and I started to understand what the weekend sale was really about.
sentences.cn: 我看着人们快速填满购物篮，开始明白周末促销到底是怎么回事了。

sentences.en: Every small purchase was a *gain* for the store, yes, but the real reward was the warm feeling of neighbours choosing us over the bigger shop down the road.
Lin peered over from across the street.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林从街对面往这边看。

maybe:1.en: A tall woman in a rain jacket stopped at our outdoor display and picked up a bag of rice crackers, then put it back, then picked it up again. She looked at me. I shrugged. She said she was trying to eat less salt. I told her, honestly, that those crackers were *maybe* the lightest option we had outside. She bought two bags.
maybe:1.cnHint: 一位顾客拿起又放下米饼好几次，我告诉她这____是我们外摆里最淡口的选择。
maybe:1.hook: She asked if we carried anything with no salt at all.
maybe:1.line: 'This is *maybe* the best deal I have seen all weekend.'

sentences.en: A tall woman in a rain jacket stopped at our outdoor display and picked up a bag of rice crackers, then put it back, then picked it up again.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着雨衣的高个子女人在我们的户外展示区停了下来，拿起一袋米饼，放下，又拿起来。

sentences.en: She looked at me.
sentences.cn: 她看向我。

sentences.en: I shrugged.
sentences.cn: 我耸了耸肩。

sentences.en: She said she was trying to eat less salt.
sentences.cn: 她说她在努力少吃盐。

sentences.en: I told her, honestly, that those crackers were *maybe* the lightest option we had outside.
She bought two bags.
sentences.cn: 她买了两袋。

huge:1.en: The Manager dragged a *huge* red banner out from the back room and asked Tang and me to hang it above the entrance. It was twice as wide as the doorway. Tang stood on a step stool; I held the other end on my toes. A passing cyclist slowed down to watch, almost rode into a bin, and then stopped to read the banner properly.
huge:1.cnHint: 店长拿出一条____的红色横幅，让我和唐帮忙挂在门口上方。
huge:1.hook: The cyclist locked their bike and walked inside without a word.
huge:1.line: 'That is a *huge* banner — the whole street can see it now.'

sentences.en: The Manager dragged a *huge* red banner out from the back room and asked Tang and me to hang it above the entrance.
It was twice as wide as the doorway.
sentences.cn: 它的宽度是门口的两倍。

sentences.en: Tang stood on a step stool; I held the other end on my toes.
sentences.cn: 阿糖站在踏脚凳上，我用脚尖撑着另一头。

sentences.en: A passing cyclist slowed down to watch, almost rode into a bin, and then stopped to read the banner properly.
sentences.cn: 一个骑自行车的人放慢速度观看，差点骑进垃圾桶，然后停下来仔细读这条横幅。

diet:1.en: A regular customer — a quiet man who always bought plain yoghurt — stood outside studying the sale table with a worried expression. He picked up a bag of chocolate biscuits, checked the back, and set it down. He told me he was on a strict *diet* and could not afford any surprises. I pointed him toward the unsweetened drinks shelf inside. He looked grateful.
diet:1.cnHint: 一位常客站在促销台前，告诉我他在严格控制____，不能乱买零食。
diet:1.hook: He paused at the door and turned back to look at the biscuits one more time.
diet:1.line: 'I am on a *diet*, so I have to be careful about everything I pick up.'

sentences.en: A regular customer — a quiet man who always bought plain yoghurt — stood outside studying the sale table with a worried expression.
sentences.cn: 一个常客——一个总是买纯酸奶的安静男人，站在外面，用担忧的表情研究着特价表。

sentences.en: He picked up a bag of chocolate biscuits, checked the back, and set it down.
sentences.cn: 他拿起一袋巧克力饼干，检查背面，放了下去。

sentences.en: He told me he was on a strict *diet* and could not afford any surprises.
I pointed him toward the unsweetened drinks shelf inside.
sentences.cn: 我指向里面无糖饮料的架子。

sentences.en: He looked grateful.
sentences.cn: 他看起来很感激。

animal:1.en: A boy pressed his face against the glass door, staring at the small shelf of toy figures near the counter. 'Which one is your favourite *animal*?' I asked, turning the tiger toward him. His eyes went wide. He pointed at the shark instead, then at his pocket, then looked up at me hopefully.
animal:1.cnHint: 一个小男孩盯着货架上的玩具，用手指了指鲨鱼，又指了指自己的口袋，眼神充满期待，好像在说他的零花钱可能不太够买____。
animal:1.hook: He reached into his pocket and pulled out something far more interesting than coins.
animal:1.line: 'That *animal* is the best one on the whole shelf,' he said firmly.

sentences.en: A boy pressed his face against the glass door, staring at the small shelf of toy figures near the counter.
sentences.cn: 一个男孩把脸贴在玻璃门上，盯着柜台附近的小玩具架。

sentences.en: 'Which one is your favourite *animal*?'
I asked, turning the tiger toward him.
sentences.cn: 我问道，转向他展示老虎。

sentences.en: His eyes went wide.
sentences.cn: 他的眼睛睁得很大。

sentences.en: He pointed at the shark instead, then at his pocket, then looked up at me hopefully.
sentences.cn: 他指向鲨鱼，然后指向他的口袋，然后抬起头用希望的眼神看我。

goal:1.en: Tang swept the area outside the door just before midnight, humming to himself. 'You seem happy,' I said through the open door. 'My *goal* this week is to keep the front step cleaner than the coffee shop next door,' he said, nodding toward the rival store across the street. He was winning, apparently.
goal:1.cnHint: 阿糖在午夜前打扫门口，他告诉我他这周的____是把台阶扫得比对面咖啡店更干净。
goal:1.hook: The coffee shop door swung open, and someone stepped out with a mop.
goal:1.line: 'My *goal* is simple: the cleanest step on this street,' Tang said.

sentences.en: Tang swept the area outside the door just before midnight, humming to himself.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在午夜前扫着门外的区域，自己哼着歌。

sentences.en: 'You seem happy,' I said through the open door.
sentences.cn: "你看起来很开心，"我通过开着的门说。

sentences.en: 'My *goal* this week is to keep the front step cleaner than the coffee shop next door,' he said, nodding toward the rival store across the street.
He was winning, apparently.
sentences.cn: 他赢了，显然。

adult:1.en: A teenager counted coins on the counter for the third time, one short for a hot drink. Behind her, a quiet man in a coat waited without a word, then slid an extra coin forward. 'An *adult* thing to do,' I thought, but said nothing. She left warm. He just nodded and bought his water.
adult:1.cnHint: 一个硬币不够的少年，被身后一个陌生____默默补上了差额，然后那人买了瓶水就走了。
adult:1.hook: I saw the same coat again the next night, but the face below it was different.
adult:1.line: 'Acting like an *adult* means you help without making a big deal,' he said quietly.

sentences.en: A teenager counted coins on the counter for the third time, one short for a hot drink.
sentences.cn: 一个少年在柜台上数了第三次硬币，缺少买热饮的钱。

sentences.en: Behind her, a quiet man in a coat waited without a word, then slid an extra coin forward.
sentences.cn: 她后面，一个穿着外套的安静男人无言地等待，然后推过来一枚额外的硬币。

sentences.en: 'An *adult* thing to do,' I thought, but said nothing.
She left warm.
sentences.cn: 她离开时是温暖的。

sentences.en: He just nodded and bought his water.
sentences.cn: 他只是点了点头，买了他的水。

poor:1.en: Lin from the rival coffee shop came in at two in the morning looking tired. 'Long night?' I asked. '*Poor* planning on my part,' she said, dropping onto the stool by the window. 'I ordered three times the cups we needed and now I have to count them all.' She bought a hot drink and stayed a while.
poor:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林深夜走进来，抱怨自己____的计划导致她要数三倍数量的杯子。
poor:1.hook: She left a sticky note on the window that I did not find until morning.
poor:1.line: '*Poor* planning is my real talent,' Lin said, and actually laughed.

sentences.en: Lin from the rival coffee shop came in at two in the morning looking tired.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在凌晨两点来了，看起来很累。

sentences.en: 'Long night?'
sentences.cn: "长夜？"

sentences.en: I asked. '*Poor* planning on my part,' she said, dropping onto the stool by the window.
'I ordered three times the cups we needed and now I have to count them all.'
sentences.cn: "我订了三倍我们需要的杯子，现在我必须把它们都数一遍。"

sentences.en: She bought a hot drink and stayed a while.
sentences.cn: 她买了一杯热饮，在这里呆了一会儿。

price:1.en: The Manager taped a new sign to the door before leaving for the evening: WEEKEND SALE — ALL DRINKS HALF *PRICE*. I read it four times. Then I looked at our stock. Then I looked at the sign again. By midnight the shelf was nearly empty, and a small crowd was still growing outside the glass.
price:1.cnHint: 店长贴出了周末半____的告示，到午夜货架已经快空了，门外还有人在排队。
price:1.hook: Someone at the back of the crowd was writing something down in a notebook.
price:1.line: 'Half *price* means we work twice as hard tonight,' I told myself.

sentences.en: The Manager taped a new sign to the door before leaving for the evening: WEEKEND SALE — ALL DRINKS HALF *PRICE*.
I read it four times.
sentences.cn: 我读了四遍。

sentences.en: Then I looked at our stock.
sentences.cn: 然后我看了看我们的库存。

sentences.en: Then I looked at the sign again.
sentences.cn: 然后我又看了看那个标志。

sentences.en: By midnight the shelf was nearly empty, and a small crowd was still growing outside the glass.
sentences.cn: 到了午夜，架子几乎空了，玻璃外还有一小群人在不断增加。

type:1.en: Tang was sorting the snack display when a regular came in and stared for a long time. 'I want the salty *type*,' the man said at last, waving at the whole row. Tang and I looked at each other. We spent ten minutes holding up bags one by one until the man nodded. He seemed very satisfied.
type:1.cnHint: 一位常客盯着零食架想了很久，只说想要咸____的那种，我和阿糖一袋一袋举给他看。
type:1.hook: He came back twenty minutes later and asked for the sweet type.
type:1.line: 'I only like this *type*,' the man said, hugging the bag to his chest.

sentences.en: Tang was sorting the snack display when a regular came in and stared for a long time.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在整理零食展示，一个常客进来盯着看了很长时间。

sentences.en: 'I want the salty *type*,' the man said at last, waving at the whole row.
Tang and I looked at each other.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我互相看了一眼。

sentences.en: We spent ten minutes holding up bags one by one until the man nodded.
sentences.cn: 我们花了十分钟一个一个地拿起袋子，直到那个男人点头。

sentences.en: He seemed very satisfied.
sentences.cn: 他看起来非常满意。

sense:1.en: Just after three in the morning a woman stood outside the door for a full minute before coming in. She walked the aisles slowly, picking nothing up. 'Can I help you?' I asked. She smiled. 'I just needed the *sense* that somewhere was still open,' she said. She bought a small juice and left looking lighter.
sense:1.cnHint: 一位女士在凌晨三点走进来，说她只是需要一种____——知道某个地方还开着。
sense:1.hook: She left her umbrella behind, though the sky outside was perfectly clear.
sense:1.line: 'Sometimes you just need the *sense* that the world is still awake,' she said.

sentences.en: Just after three in the morning a woman stood outside the door for a full minute before coming in.
sentences.cn: 凌晨三点刚过，一个女人在门外站了整整一分钟才进来。

sentences.en: She walked the aisles slowly, picking nothing up.
sentences.cn: 她缓缓走过走道，什么都没拿起来。

sentences.en: 'Can I help you?'
sentences.cn: "我能帮你吗？"

sentences.en: I asked.
sentences.cn: 我问。

sentences.en: She smiled.
sentences.cn: 她微笑了。

sentences.en: 'I just needed the *sense* that somewhere was still open,' she said.
She bought a small juice and left looking lighter.
sentences.cn: 她买了一小杯果汁就离开了，看起来轻松多了。

rate:1.en: Lin leaned on the counter at dawn, comparing notes on foot traffic. 'Your sale *rate* last night was incredible,' she said, sounding slightly impressed and slightly annoyed. 'Half-price drinks,' I said. She was quiet for a moment. Then: 'I might hate you a little.' She bought two drinks and left smiling anyway.
rate:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在黎明时分过来，提到我们昨晚的销售____很惊人，然后说她可能有点恨我们。
rate:1.hook: She came back an hour later with a sign of her own and taped it to her window.
rate:1.line: 'That sale *rate* should be illegal,' Lin said, but she was smiling.

sentences.en: Lin leaned on the counter at dawn, comparing notes on foot traffic.
sentences.cn: 林在黎明时倚在柜台上，比较脚流量的笔记。

sentences.en: 'Your sale *rate* last night was incredible,' she said, sounding slightly impressed and slightly annoyed.
'Half-price drinks,' I said.
sentences.cn: "半价饮料，"我说。

sentences.en: She was quiet for a moment.
sentences.cn: 她沉默了一会儿。

sentences.en: Then: 'I might hate you a little.'
sentences.cn: 然后："我可能有点恨你。"

sentences.en: She bought two drinks and left smiling anyway.
sentences.cn: 她买了两杯饮料，不过还是面带微笑地离开了。

within:1.en: The Manager taped a bright sign to our door: everything on the front shelf was on sale. 'All items must be sold *within* two hours,' he told me, tapping his watch. By the time I looked up, a woman in a yellow coat had already cleared half the shelf without a word.
within:1.cnHint: 店长规定促销商品必须在两小时____售完，一位黄衣女士动作极快。
within:1.hook: She came back an hour later, and she was not alone.
within:1.line: 'All discounts must be used *within* today, so hurry!' said the Manager.

sentences.en: The Manager taped a bright sign to our door: everything on the front shelf was on sale.
sentences.cn: 店长在我们的门上贴了一个醒目的标志：前架子上的所有东西都在打折。

sentences.en: 'All items must be sold *within* two hours,' he told me, tapping his watch.
By the time I looked up, a woman in a yellow coat had already cleared half the shelf without a word.
sentences.cn: 到我抬起头时，一个穿着黄色外套的女人已经没有言语地清空了一半的架子。

either:1.en: Lin from the shop across the street leaned in our doorway during the sale rush. 'Your prices are lower, but your coffee isn't good,' he said with a shrug. I didn't argue. He didn't leave, *either*. He just stood there, slowly eating one of our discounted meat buns.
either:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林虽然嘴上挑剔，却____没有离开，站着吃起了打折肉包。
either:1.hook: He left a small note on the counter before he finally walked out.
either:1.line: 'I do not like your layout, and I do not trust your coffee, *either*,' said Lin.

sentences.en: Lin from the shop across the street leaned in our doorway during the sale rush.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在销售高峰期时靠在我们的门框上。

sentences.en: 'Your prices are lower, but your coffee isn't good,' he said with a shrug.
sentences.cn: "你们的价格便宜，但咖啡不好喝，"他耸了耸肩说。

sentences.en: I didn't argue.
sentences.cn: 我没有反驳。

sentences.en: He didn't leave, *either*.
He just stood there, slowly eating one of our discounted meat buns.
sentences.cn: 他就这么站在那里，慢慢咀嚼着我们打折的肉包。

various:1.en: For the weekend sale, the Manager had stacked *various* snacks near the door — chips, dried fruit, little cakes, and things I couldn't name. Each bag had a cheerful red tag. A boy stopped in front of the display for a very long time, clearly doing very serious math in his head.
various:1.cnHint: 促销期间店门口摆满了____各式各样的零食，一个小男孩站在那里默默地计算着。
various:1.hook: He pulled out a tiny notebook before choosing anything.
various:1.line: 'I put out *various* snacks so every kind of customer finds something,' said the Manager.

sentences.en: For the weekend sale, the Manager had stacked *various* snacks near the door — chips, dried fruit, little cakes, and things I couldn't name.
Each bag had a cheerful red tag.
sentences.cn: 每个袋子上都贴着一张欢快的红色标签。

sentences.en: A boy stopped in front of the display for a very long time, clearly doing very serious math in his head.
sentences.cn: 一个男孩在展示柜前站了很久，显然在脑子里做着非常认真的数学题。

main:1.en: Tang pointed at the street outside and said the *main* reason people stopped at our store was the corner position — easy to see, easy to reach. I watched the door all evening and decided she was right. But one old man walked past four times before coming in, as if making up his mind.
main:1.cnHint: 阿糖说地理位置是顾客光顾的____原因，但有位老人在门外来回走了四次。
main:1.hook: When he finally entered, he asked for something we didn't carry.
main:1.line: 'The *main* reason this store works is the corner — people see us first,' said Tang.

sentences.en: Tang pointed at the street outside and said the *main* reason people stopped at our store was the corner position — easy to see, easy to reach.
I watched the door all evening and decided she was right.
sentences.cn: 我整个晚上都盯着门，觉得她说得没错。

sentences.en: But one old man walked past four times before coming in, as if making up his mind.
sentences.cn: 但有个老头走过了四次才进来，好像在下决心。

employee:1.en: A woman stopped me near the entrance and asked if I was a new *employee*. I said yes, just started this week. She smiled and said she had seen four new clerks in two years. She said it in a kind way, not a worried one. Then she bought a single piece of gum and left.
employee:1.cnHint: 一位女顾客问我是不是新来的____，她说两年内她见过四个新店员了。
employee:1.hook: She turned back at the door and added one last quiet remark.
employee:1.line: 'So you are the new *employee*? The Manager always picks the night shift ones carefully,' she said.

sentences.en: A woman stopped me near the entrance and asked if I was a new *employee*.
I said yes, just started this week.
sentences.cn: 我说是的，这周刚开始上班。

sentences.en: She smiled and said she had seen four new clerks in two years.
sentences.cn: 她笑着说她两年内见过四个新员工。

sentences.en: She said it in a kind way, not a worried one.
sentences.cn: 她用善良的语气说这话，而不是担忧的。

sentences.en: Then she bought a single piece of gum and left.
sentences.cn: 然后她只买了一块口香糖就走了。

class:1.en: Three students spilled in after midnight, still in the middle of a loud debate. One of them slapped the counter and said their study *class* had just ended and they needed sugar immediately. I sold them three of everything sweet we had. They left still arguing, but happier.
class:1.cnHint: 三个学生深夜冲进来，说他们的补习____刚结束，急需补充糖分。
class:1.hook: One of them left a folded piece of paper near the register.
class:1.line: 'Our exam prep *class* just ended — we survived, so we deserve snacks,' said one student.

sentences.en: Three students spilled in after midnight, still in the middle of a loud debate.
sentences.cn: 三个学生在午夜后冲了进来，还在激烈地争论着什么。

sentences.en: One of them slapped the counter and said their study *class* had just ended and they needed sugar immediately.
I sold them three of everything sweet we had.
sentences.cn: 我把店里所有的甜味零食各卖了三份给他们。

sentences.en: They left still arguing, but happier.
sentences.cn: 他们边争论边走了，但看起来更开心了。

behavior:1.en: Tang quietly pulled me aside after a customer left the store without paying for a small drink. 'Watch the door,' she said. 'It's not the first time.' She wasn't angry — just calm, like she had seen every kind of *behavior* in this store and none of it surprised her anymore.
behavior:1.cnHint: 一位顾客没付钱就走了，阿糖平静地说她见过各种各样的____，早已不觉得奇怪。
behavior:1.hook: The same customer returned twenty minutes later with exact change.
behavior:1.line: 'In this store you see every kind of *behavior* — the night shift teaches you fast,' said Tang.

sentences.en: Tang quietly pulled me aside after a customer left the store without paying for a small drink.
sentences.cn: 一个顾客离开后没有付一杯小饮料的钱，阿糖悄悄把我拉到一边。

sentences.en: 'Watch the door,' she said.
sentences.cn: "看好门，"她说。

sentences.en: 'It's not the first time.'
sentences.cn: "这不是第一次了。"

sentences.en: She wasn't angry — just calm, like she had seen every kind of *behavior* in this store and none of it surprised her anymore.

disease:1.en: An older man bought three bottles of herbal drink and told me his doctor said stress was a modern *disease* worse than a cold. He looked very unbothered for someone worried about stress. He tucked the bottles into a tote bag, patted the counter twice, and walked into the dark street.
disease:1.cnHint: 一位老先生说医生告诉他压力是一种现代____，但他本人看起来十分淡定。
disease:1.hook: The label on one of his bottles was handwritten, not printed.
disease:1.line: 'My doctor says stress is a *disease*, so I buy these every Friday without fail,' the old man said.

sentences.en: An older man bought three bottles of herbal drink and told me his doctor said stress was a modern *disease* worse than a cold.
He looked very unbothered for someone worried about stress.
sentences.cn: 对于一个担心压力的人来说，他看起来毫不在意。

sentences.en: He tucked the bottles into a tote bag, patted the counter twice, and walked into the dark street.
sentences.cn: 他把那些瓶子塞进一个手提袋里，在柜台上拍了两下，然后走进了黑暗的街道。

action:1.en: The Manager taped a big red sign to the door before sunrise. 'Weekend sale starts now,' he said, clapping his hands. 'We need *action*, not standing around.' I grabbed a mop, Tang grabbed a price gun, and somehow the tiny store felt like the centre of the whole street.
action:1.cnHint: 店长要求大家赶紧____起来，备战周末促销。
action:1.hook: Then a figure across the street began writing something on a chalkboard.
action:1.line: 'We need *action*, not standing around — move those displays outside now!'

sentences.en: The Manager taped a big red sign to the door before sunrise.
sentences.cn: 店长在日出前把一张大红色的标志贴在门上。

sentences.en: 'Weekend sale starts now,' he said, clapping his hands.
sentences.cn: "周末促销现在开始，"他拍了拍手说。

sentences.en: 'We need *action*, not standing around.'
I grabbed a mop, Tang grabbed a price gun, and somehow the tiny store felt like the centre of the whole street.
sentences.cn: 我拿起了拖把，阿糖拿起了标价枪，不知怎么地，这个小小的店铺感觉像是整条街的中心。

program:1.en: Tang had written a whole *program* for the weekend sale on the back of a receipt: greet customers, push the two-for-one drinks, offer free bags. It was only eight steps, but she spoke about it like a general reading a battle plan. I memorised every line.
program:1.cnHint: 阿糖制定了一份详细的促销____，每一步都清清楚楚。
program:1.hook: Step seven had a small star next to it, but Tang would not explain why.
program:1.line: 'Follow the *program* exactly and we will be fine — trust me on step seven.'

sentences.en: Tang had written a whole *program* for the weekend sale on the back of a receipt: greet customers, push the two-for-one drinks, offer free bags.
It was only eight steps, but she spoke about it like a general reading a battle plan.
sentences.cn: 她用一种像将军读战斗计划一样的语气讲述这件事。

sentences.en: I memorised every line.
sentences.cn: 我把每一句都记住了。

situation:1.en: By nine in the morning the pavement outside was crowded with shoppers and the queue reached the door. I looked at Tang, unsure what to do. She took one glance at the *situation* and opened the second register without a word. I felt grateful and slightly embarrassed.
situation:1.cnHint: 早上九点，门口排起了长队，阿糖迅速判断了____并打开了第二台收银机。
situation:1.hook: One customer at the back of the queue kept checking the store across the street.
situation:1.line: 'The *situation* is under control — just keep smiling and scan faster.'

sentences.en: By nine in the morning the pavement outside was crowded with shoppers and the queue reached the door.
sentences.cn: 到了上午九点，店外的人行道上挤满了购物者，队伍一直排到门口。

sentences.en: I looked at Tang, unsure what to do.
sentences.cn: 我看着阿糖，不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: She took one glance at the *situation* and opened the second register without a word.
I felt grateful and slightly embarrassed.
sentences.cn: 我既感到感谢，又有点尴尬。

order:1.en: A man in a raincoat handed me a handwritten list: six rice balls, four teas, two hot soups. 'It is a standing *order* every Saturday,' Tang whispered. 'He never changes it.' I packed everything in two minutes flat and felt oddly proud of my speed.
order:1.cnHint: 一位穿雨衣的顾客每周六都有固定____，内容一成不变。
order:1.hook: This time he lingered by the door, glancing at a note in his hand.
order:1.line: 'Same *order* as last week, please — you will get used to me soon enough.'

sentences.en: A man in a raincoat handed me a handwritten list: six rice balls, four teas, two hot soups.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着雨衣的男人递给我一张手写的清单：六个饭团，四杯茶，两碗热汤。

sentences.en: 'It is a standing *order* every Saturday,' Tang whispered.
'He never changes it.'
sentences.cn: "他从不改变，"她说。

sentences.en: I packed everything in two minutes flat and felt oddly proud of my speed.
sentences.cn: 我在两分钟内打好了所有东西，莫名地为自己的速度感到骄傲。

event:1.en: The Manager had printed flyers calling the weekend sale a 'community *event*.' That felt grand for a store the size of a parking space, but people did come — neighbours with tote bags, students with coins, an old man who just wanted somewhere warm to stand for a while.
event:1.cnHint: 店长把周末促销称为一场社区____，吸引了各种各样的街坊邻居。
event:1.hook: The old man in the corner had not bought anything yet, but he kept smiling at the door.
event:1.line: 'Welcome to our little *event* — there is a free sample by the register.'

sentences.en: The Manager had printed flyers calling the weekend sale a 'community *event*.'
That felt grand for a store the size of a parking space, but people did come — neighbours with tote bags, students with coins, an old man who just wanted somewhere warm to stand for a while.
sentences.cn: 对于一个停车位大小的店铺来说，这感觉很盛大，但人们确实来了——拿着手提袋的邻居、拿着硬币的学生，还有一个只是想站在温暖地方的老头。

account:1.en: Lin from the store across the street strolled in at noon, phone raised, filming everything. 'Research,' she said sweetly. Tang gave a slow blink. Later the Manager said Lin had posted an *account* of our sale online, calling our prices 'surprisingly reasonable.' Tang printed it and stuck it on the fridge.
account:1.cnHint: 对面店的隔壁咖啡店的林在网上发布了一篇对我们促销活动的____，措辞出人意料地友好。
account:1.hook: But Lin had circled something in the post with a red pen before she left.
account:1.line: 'I posted a fair *account* — your dumplings really are better than I expected.'

sentences.en: Lin from the store across the street strolled in at noon, phone raised, filming everything.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林中午闲庭信步走了进来，手机举得高高的，什么都要拍。

sentences.en: 'Research,' she said sweetly.
sentences.cn: "做功课呢，"她甜蜜蜜地说。

sentences.en: Tang gave a slow blink.
sentences.cn: 阿糖慢吞吞地眨了眨眼。

sentences.en: Later the Manager said Lin had posted an *account* of our sale online, calling our prices 'surprisingly reasonable.'
Tang printed it and stuck it on the fridge.
sentences.cn: 阿糖把它打印出来，贴在了冰箱上。

deal:1.en: A student emptied her pockets on the counter: coins, a crumpled bill, a bus pass. She needed one more yuan for the meal set. I paused, then quietly took one yuan from the small tips jar beside the register. 'That is a *deal*,' I said. She beamed so wide I forgot I was tired.
deal:1.cnHint: 一个学生差一元钱，我悄悄补上，达成了这笔____。
deal:1.hook: She came back twenty minutes later and left something small on the counter without a word.
deal:1.line: 'That is a *deal* — and please come back when you have more coins next time.'

sentences.en: A student emptied her pockets on the counter: coins, a crumpled bill, a bus pass.
sentences.cn: 一个女生把口袋掏空了放在柜台上：硬币、一张皱巴巴的纸币、一张公交卡。

sentences.en: She needed one more yuan for the meal set.
sentences.cn: 她还差一块钱才能买套餐。

sentences.en: I paused, then quietly took one yuan from the small tips jar beside the register.
sentences.cn: 我停顿了一下，然后悄悄从收银机旁边的小费罐里拿出一块钱。

sentences.en: 'That is a *deal*,' I said.
She beamed so wide I forgot I was tired.
sentences.cn: 她笑得特别开心，我一下子忘了自己有多累。

degree:1.en: The soup machine broke at two in the afternoon and the temperature inside the cups dropped to a useless *degree*. The Manager poked it twice and sighed. Tang found a power switch behind a shelf and the machine hummed back to life. The Manager stared at the shelf for a long moment.
degree:1.cnHint: 汤机坏了，温度降到了没用的____，阿糖找到了隐藏的开关解决了问题。
degree:1.hook: The Manager quietly moved three boxes to check what else might be hiding behind that shelf.
degree:1.line: 'The temperature had dropped to a *degree* where nobody would buy it — good catch, Tang.'

sentences.en: The soup machine broke at two in the afternoon and the temperature inside the cups dropped to a useless *degree*.
The Manager poked it twice and sighed.
sentences.cn: 店长戳了戳机器，叹了口气。

sentences.en: Tang found a power switch behind a shelf and the machine hummed back to life.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在货架后面找到了一个电源开关，机器嗡嗡嗡活过来了。

sentences.en: The Manager stared at the shelf for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 店长盯着那个货架看了很久。

worker:1.en: Saturday morning, a road crew blocked half the street outside the store. One *worker* in an orange vest kept waving cars away from a broken pipe. I watched from behind the glass door, holding a mop I did not need, glad the noise stayed outside.
worker:1.cnHint: 一名施工____挡在店门口，让早班变得格外热闹。
worker:1.hook: Then he stepped inside, mud on his boots and urgency in his eyes.
worker:1.line: 'Excuse me — I'm a *worker* out there, can I use your phone?'

sentences.en: Saturday morning, a road crew blocked half the street outside the store.
sentences.cn: 星期六上午，一支道路施工队把街道外面的半边都堵住了。

sentences.en: One *worker* in an orange vest kept waving cars away from a broken pipe.
I watched from behind the glass door, holding a mop I did not need, glad the noise stayed outside.
sentences.cn: 我透过玻璃门往外看，手里拿着根本用不上的拖把，庆幸噪音都留在了外面。

control:1.en: A small dog tied to the bike rack outside went wild every time someone walked past. Its owner, an older man buying instant noodles, rushed out three times to calm it. By the third trip I could see he was losing *control* of both the dog and his temper.
control:1.cnHint: 门外那条小狗完全不受____，主人跑进跑出好几回。
control:1.hook: On the fourth bark, something on the noodle shelf came crashing down.
control:1.line: 'I'm sorry — I just can't *control* him when he smells food.'

sentences.en: A small dog tied to the bike rack outside went wild every time someone walked past.
sentences.cn: 拴在自行车架上的一只小狗，每次有人经过都要发疯。

sentences.en: Its owner, an older man buying instant noodles, rushed out three times to calm it.
sentences.cn: 它的主人，一个买速冻面的老大爷，跑出去三次去安抚它。

sentences.en: By the third trip I could see he was losing *control* of both the dog and his temper.

product:1.en: A woman set up a small folding table right outside our door and began showing neighbours a bottle of thick green liquid. She called it a miracle *product* that could clean anything. The Manager watched through the window, arms crossed, saying nothing — which was somehow worse than saying something.
product:1.cnHint: 一位女士在门口推销一款神奇____，把店长气得沉默不语。
product:1.hook: Then she held the bottle up next to our store sign and smiled at a passing camera.
product:1.line: 'This *product* will outsell everything in that store, I promise you.'

sentences.en: A woman set up a small folding table right outside our door and began showing neighbours a bottle of thick green liquid.
sentences.cn: 一个女人在我们门外摆了一张小折叠桌，开始给邻居们展示一瓶粘稠的绿色液体。

sentences.en: She called it a miracle *product* that could clean anything.
The Manager watched through the window, arms crossed, saying nothing — which was somehow worse than saying something.
sentences.cn: 店长从窗户往外看，双手交叉，什么都没说——这样反而比说什么都更糟糕。

practice:1.en: Every Sunday a teenager sat on the low wall across from us and played a small keyboard through a tiny speaker. It was his outdoor *practice* spot, he said, because his mum banned noise at home after nine. The notes floated in each time someone opened our door.
practice:1.cnHint: 一个少年把我们店门口当作他的户外____场地，每周都来报到。
practice:1.hook: Tonight he stopped mid-song and stared at something above the store roof.
practice:1.line: 'I come here to *practice* because nobody shouts at me outside.'

sentences.en: Every Sunday a teenager sat on the low wall across from us and played a small keyboard through a tiny speaker.
sentences.cn: 每个星期天，有个少年坐在我们对面的矮墙上，用一个小音箱放着一架小键盘。

sentences.en: It was his outdoor *practice* spot, he said, because his mum banned noise at home after nine.
The notes floated in each time someone opened our door.
sentences.cn: 每次有人打开我们的门，乐声就飘进来。

environment:1.en: A city inspector walked slowly past the store, taking notes on a clipboard. She paused to look at our bin area, then at the cracked pavement, then at the bright lights above the door. 'The *environment* here affects everyone on the street,' she said, half to me and half to herself.
environment:1.cnHint: 一位检查员在门外评估街道____，顺带打量了我们的店面。
environment:1.hook: She circled something on her clipboard twice before walking away.
environment:1.line: 'A clean *environment* outside your store matters more than you think.'

sentences.en: A city inspector walked slowly past the store, taking notes on a clipboard.
sentences.cn: 一个城市检查员缓缓走过店铺，在记事板上记笔记。

sentences.en: She paused to look at our bin area, then at the cracked pavement, then at the bright lights above the door.
sentences.cn: 她停下来看了看我们的垃圾桶区，然后看看裂了的人行道，再看看门上方明亮的灯。

sentences.en: 'The *environment* here affects everyone on the street,' she said, half to me and half to herself.

system:1.en: Just before midnight the traffic lights at our corner went dark. No green, no red — nothing. Drivers crept forward, unsure who should go. A delivery rider told me the whole signal *system* in this block had tripped. I stood in the doorway watching the polite, slow chaos unfold.
system:1.cnHint: 路口的红绿灯____突然失灵，深夜的街角乱成一锅粥。
system:1.hook: Then one very confident car simply did not slow down at all.
system:1.line: 'The whole light *system* is down — I've already called it in.'

sentences.en: Just before midnight the traffic lights at our corner went dark.
sentences.cn: 午夜刚过，我们这个路口的红绿灯暗了。

sentences.en: No green, no red — nothing.
sentences.cn: 没有绿灯，没有红灯——什么都没有。

sentences.en: Drivers crept forward, unsure who should go.
sentences.cn: 司机们小心翼翼地往前爬，不知道谁该先走。

sentences.en: A delivery rider told me the whole signal *system* in this block had tripped.
I stood in the doorway watching the polite, slow chaos unfold.
sentences.cn: 我站在门框里，看着这场彬彬有礼、缓慢无序的混乱展开。

natural:1.en: After a short rain the street smelled like wet concrete and something green from the small trees by the kerb. A regular customer stopped under our awning, closed his eyes, and breathed in slowly. 'That smell is so *natural*,' he said, looking almost happy for the first time I had seen.
natural:1.cnHint: 一场小雨后，一位常客在门口深吸一口____的气息，神情放松。
natural:1.hook: Then he opened his eyes and handed me a very damp shopping list.
natural:1.line: 'Nothing beats that *natural* smell after rain, don't you think?'

sentences.en: After a short rain the street smelled like wet concrete and something green from the small trees by the kerb.
sentences.cn: 下过小雨以后，街道闻起来像湿漉漉的混凝土，还有路边小树传来的青草味。

sentences.en: A regular customer stopped under our awning, closed his eyes, and breathed in slowly.
sentences.cn: 一个常客停在我们的遮阳棚下，闭上眼睛，慢慢吸了一口气。

sentences.en: 'That smell is so *natural*,' he said, looking almost happy for the first time I had seen.

free:1.en: A woman was handing out small paper fans on the pavement, each printed with a cartoon cat. 'Completely *free*,' she told everyone who passed, smiling wide. Most people took one without stopping. I got one too, through the door, and used it to fan the warm air near the register all night.
free:1.cnHint: 一位女士在门外派发____的纸扇，连我也收到了一把。
free:1.hook: By midnight I noticed every fan had a tiny phone number printed on the back.
free:1.line: 'Take one — it's totally *free*, no catch at all!'

sentences.en: A woman was handing out small paper fans on the pavement, each printed with a cartoon cat.
sentences.cn: 一个女人在人行道上派发小纸扇，上面都印着卡通猫。

sentences.en: 'Completely *free*,' she told everyone who passed, smiling wide.
Most people took one without stopping.
sentences.cn: 大多数人都不停地拿了一把。

sentences.en: I got one too, through the door, and used it to fan the warm air near the register all night.
sentences.cn: 我也从门那边要到了一把，整晚用它来给收银台附近的热空气扇风。

mind:1.en: The Saturday sale turned the quiet street outside into a small river of people. I stepped out to fix a fallen sign, and the noise hit me at once. A woman stopped, closed her eyes, and took a slow breath. 'I have to *mind* my thoughts,' she said, 'or the crowd pulls them away.' She bought nothing, just smiled and walked on.
mind:1.cnHint: 促销日街上人群嘈杂，一位女士驻足，说她需要____自己的思绪，然后微笑离去。
mind:1.hook: She came back an hour later, bought one small notebook, and said nothing.
mind:1.line: 'I have to *mind* my thoughts, or the crowd pulls them away.'

sentences.en: The Saturday sale turned the quiet street outside into a small river of people.
sentences.cn: 星期六的促销把安静的街道变成了人的小河。

sentences.en: I stepped out to fix a fallen sign, and the noise hit me at once.
sentences.cn: 我走出去扶起一块掉下来的招牌，噪音一下子砸了过来。

sentences.en: A woman stopped, closed her eyes, and took a slow breath.
sentences.cn: 一个女人停下来，闭上眼睛，深深吸了一口气。

sentences.en: 'I have to *mind* my thoughts,' she said, 'or the crowd pulls them away.'
She bought nothing, just smiled and walked on.
sentences.cn: 她什么都没买，只是笑着走了。

rise:1.en: By ten in the morning the number of people on the street corner had seen a sharp *rise*. I watched from the doorway as the crowd pushed past our small A-board sign. Tang appeared beside me, arms full of extra stock. 'Every big sale weekend is the same,' she said. 'Enjoy the calm while it lasts.'
rise:1.cnHint: 周末促销，街角人流量出现明显____，同事唐提醒我趁早享受片刻安静。
rise:1.hook: Then a man with a very large cart appeared around the corner, heading straight for us.
rise:1.line: 'Every big sale weekend sees a *rise* like this — enjoy the calm while it lasts.'

sentences.en: By ten in the morning the number of people on the street corner had seen a sharp *rise*.
I watched from the doorway as the crowd pushed past our small A-board sign.
sentences.cn: 我从门口看着人群从我们那个小标牌前涌过。

sentences.en: Tang appeared beside me, arms full of extra stock.
sentences.cn: 阿糖出现在我身边，怀里抱满了额外的货。

sentences.en: 'Every big sale weekend is the same,' she said.
sentences.cn: 每个大促销周末都是这样，她说。

sentences.en: 'Enjoy the calm while it lasts.'
sentences.cn: 趁着还没那么忙，好好享受一下吧。

prove:1.en: Lin from the shop across the road set up a bright outdoor display right opposite ours. The Manager watched through the window, arms folded. 'They want to *prove* they have better prices,' he said quietly. I stacked our own sale items a little straighter and hoped he was wrong. The street hummed around us.
prove:1.cnHint: 对面的林摆出促销展示，店长说对方想____自己价格更低，我默默把货物摆得更整齐。
prove:1.hook: A customer stood between both displays for a long moment, then turned toward our door.
prove:1.line: 'They just want to *prove* their prices are better — we'll show them otherwise.'

sentences.en: Lin from the shop across the road set up a bright outdoor display right opposite ours.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在街对面支起了一个亮眼的户外展示，正好对着我们的。

sentences.en: The Manager watched through the window, arms folded.
sentences.cn: 店长从窗口看着，抱着胳膊。

sentences.en: 'They want to *prove* they have better prices,' he said quietly.
I stacked our own sale items a little straighter and hoped he was wrong.
sentences.cn: 我把我们自己的促销商品码得直直的，希望他说错了。

sentences.cn: 门边有个高个子男人用一种微妙、心领神会的笑容看着我们。

almost:2.en: I was restocking the top shelf when a small tin slipped from my hand and fell behind the fridge. I reached in and pulled out the tin — and *almost* dropped it again when I saw what was taped to its bottom: a folded note with a name and a phone number written in careful, old-fashioned letters. Tang glanced over, eyebrows raised. Neither of us recognised the name.
almost:2.cnHint: 我在冰柜后找回一个小铁罐，看到罐底贴着一张字条时____吓了一跳，阿糖也认不出上面写的名字。
almost:2.hook: The number, Tang said softly, had not worked for at least five years.
almost:2.line: 'I *almost* missed it — it was hidden right at the back.'

sentences.en: I was restocking the top shelf when a small tin slipped from my hand and fell behind the fridge.

especially:2.en: The Manager had decorated the store for the weekend sale — little paper stars on every shelf, a cheerful hand-drawn banner above the door. It looked *especially* bright against the dark street outside. I stood by the window watching people slow down as they passed, drawn in by the light. Tang brought two cups of warm tea. One regular stopped, pressed her face to the glass, and grinned like a child.
especially:2.cnHint: 店长为周末大促装点了小店，橱窗在黑夜中____耀眼，一位常客贴着玻璃往里张望，笑得像个孩子。
especially:2.hook: She came in every night, Tang whispered, but had never once bought anything.
especially:2.line: 'It looks *especially* lovely tonight — better than any other weekend.'

sentences.en: The Manager had decorated the store for the weekend sale — little paper stars on every shelf, a cheerful hand-drawn banner above the door.

sentences.cn: 一位常客停下来，把脸贴在玻璃上，像小孩一样咧嘴笑。

publish:2.en: I noticed a neatly folded newspaper left on the counter beside the card reader. Someone had circled a small article with a red pen. The headline read: LOCAL STORE CLERK TO *PUBLISH* COLLECTION OF NIGHT STORIES. There was no photo, only a name — and when Tang walked over and read it, they went very still. The Manager came out of the back room with a strange expression.
publish:2.cnHint: 柜台上有人留下一份报纸，上面用红笔圈出一篇文章——一位便利店夜班店员即将____一本故事集，阿糖看完后久久没有说话。
publish:2.hook: The name in the article was someone none of us had ever heard of — or so we thought.
publish:2.line: 'They are going to *publish* it next month — the night stories from this very street.'

sentences.en: I noticed a neatly folded newspaper left on the counter beside the card reader.
sentences.cn: 我注意到柜台旁边放着一份整整齐齐叠好的报纸，就在塔罗牌读者的旁边。

sentences.en: Someone had circled a small article with a red pen.
sentences.cn: 有人用红笔圈了一篇很小的文章。

sentences.en: The headline read: LOCAL STORE CLERK TO *PUBLISH* COLLECTION OF NIGHT STORIES.
There was no photo, only a name — and when Tang walked over and read it, they went very still.
sentences.cn: 当阿糖走过去读到那个名字时，整个人都僵住了。

sentences.en: The Manager came out of the back room with a strange expression.
sentences.cn: 店长从后间走出来，表情很奇怪。

activity:2.en: The Manager had planned a small in-store *activity* for Saturday night: guess the number of sweets in a jar and win a discount. By two in the morning the jar was surrounded by torn slips of paper. I counted forty-one entries. Tang was adding them up at the counter when a delivery driver leaned in from the doorway, looked at the jar, and quietly wrote a number on a slip without saying a word.
activity:2.cnHint: 店长为周末大促策划了一个猜糖果数量的____，一位送货司机悄悄走进来，默默写下一个数字后转身离去。
activity:2.hook: His number was exactly right — but he never came back to claim the prize.
activity:2.line: 'This little *activity* brings more people in than any sale sign ever did.'

science:2.en: A young man spread his notes across the whole snack counter, textbook open to a chapter on *science* — something about light and waves, I could see the diagrams from where I stood. He ordered a hot drink and did not look up for an hour. Tang refilled his cup without being asked. As he finally packed his bag to leave, he tucked a small folded paper under the empty cup.
science:2.cnHint: 一个年轻人把课本摊开在零食柜台上复习____，阿糖悄悄给他续了杯热饮，他离开时在杯子下压了一张折叠的小纸条。
science:2.hook: The note had only four words on it, and none of them were about science.
science:2.line: '*Science* makes more sense at two in the morning, somehow.'

sentences.en: A young man spread his notes across the whole snack counter, textbook open to a chapter on *science* — something about light and waves, I could see the diagrams from where I stood.

sentences.cn: 他点了杯热饮，一个小时没抬过头。

sentences.en: Tang refilled his cup without being asked.
sentences.cn: 阿糖没等他开口就给他续上了杯子。

sentences.cn: 他最后收拾好包包准备离开时，在空杯子底下塞了一张折叠起来的纸条。

personal:2.en: A folded note had been left under the counter, addressed to nobody in particular. The Manager picked it up and read it twice, his face going very still. 'This is *personal*,' he said quietly, sliding it into his shirt pocket before Tang or I could see a single word.
personal:2.cnHint: 店长在柜台下发现一张折好的纸条，神情变得凝重，说这是____的事。
personal:2.hook: But his hands would not stop shaking all night.
personal:2.line: 'This is *personal* — please don't ask me about it.'

rather:2.en: The stockroom smelled *rather* odd that morning — not bad exactly, but strange, like old paper and something sweet. Tang sniffed the air and said nothing. I found a cardboard box in the corner, sealed with too much tape. Nobody remembered ordering it, and the delivery note had no sender name.
rather:2.cnHint: 库房里有一股____奇怪的气味，角落里出现了一个没有寄件人信息的箱子。
rather:2.hook: The box was warm to the touch.
rather:2.line: 'It smells *rather* strange in here, don't you think?'

sentences.en: The stockroom smelled *rather* odd that morning — not bad exactly, but strange, like old paper and something sweet.
Tang sniffed the air and said nothing.

instead:2.en: Lin was supposed to drop off the weekend stock report, but she never came through the front door. *Instead*, a small sealed envelope appeared on the mat, pushed under the gap, with only my name written on it in red pen. No explanation. No knock. Just silence outside.
instead:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林没有按约定送来报告，____在门缝下出现了一封写着我名字的红字信封。
instead:2.hook: I was almost sure I heard footsteps running away.
instead:2.line: 'I did not call you — I left a note *instead*.'

sentences.en: Lin was supposed to drop off the weekend stock report, but she never came through the front door.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林应该来送周末库存报告，但她没从前门进来。

performance:2.en: A regular customer, an older man who always bought warm tea, paused at the door and pinned a small flyer to our notice board. percent:2.en: Tang pointed at the small screen behind the counter. 'Sales are up forty *percent* from last Saturday,' she said, sounding surprised. percent:2.hook: Nobody heard what the Manager said inside.
percent:2.line: 'Sales are up forty *percent* — how is that even possible?'

power:2.en: The lights flickered once, then went out completely. In the sudden dark, Tang grabbed a torch from under the counter without a word — she had clearly done this before. power:2.cnHint: 促销周末____突然断了，阿糖镇定地从柜台下摸出手电筒，说这种事每次大促都会发生。
power:2.hook: Then someone knocked hard on the locked front door.

sentences.cn: 突然黑下来时，阿糖没有任何迟疑地从柜台下面抄起手电筒——她显然做过很多次。

encourage:2.en: The weekend sale turned the store into a small storm of shopping baskets and loud opinions. I fumbled with the price-gun and tagged a bag of chips at ten times the real cost. sentences.cn: 反而，她拍了拍我的肩膀，说出了我当时最需要听的话。

sentences.en: It meant a lot to have someone *encourage* me rather than laugh.

travel:2.en: An old man came in just after two in the morning, rolling a large suitcase behind him. He bought a hot meat bun and ate it standing by the window, staring at the dark street. travel:2.hook: He left a small photograph on the counter and did not come back for it.

chance:2.en: Lin came in just before three, carrying a tray of sample snacks from the new store down the street. He set them on the counter and smiled at me like we were old friends. quite:2.en: By four in the morning the rush was over and the store felt *quite* different — still and warm, with the hum of the drink fridges filling the silence. I wiped down the counter and found myself enjoying it. One regular sat in the corner reading a thick book he had bought here every week for a month. I had never once seen him reach the last page.

quite:2.hook: Tonight, for the first time, I noticed he was reading it backwards.
quite:2.line: 'It is *quite* peaceful here after the crowds leave, is it not?'

technology:2.hook: The teenager then asked if I knew who had left a voice message on the store's old phone.
technology:2.line: 'All this *technology* and people still queue for the human till — funny, right?'

sentences.en: She said, 'I just need a moment to think.'
sentences.cn: 她说："我就想静静地想一下。"

sentences.en: I have seen busy people and tired people, but her *situation* felt different — like she was solving something much bigger than a late-night snack run.
She bought nothing.
sentences.cn: 她什么也没买。

sentences.en: She just left a folded note on the counter.
sentences.cn: 只是在柜台上留了一张折好的纸条。

order:2.en: The delivery boxes arrived early and in no sensible *order*: chips on top of bread, cold drinks beside the hot-food shelf, three boxes marked FRAGILE stacked at the very bottom. I spent an hour sorting everything before the morning rush. When the Manager checked at six, she nodded once and said nothing. That nod felt like a gold medal. Then she pointed at one box I had missed behind the mop bucket.
order:2.cnHint: 送货箱子到了，但____全乱了，我花了一个小时整理，店长点了点头，但又指向了我漏掉的一个箱子。
order:2.hook: Inside that last box was something the invoice did not list.
order:2.line: 'Please put these in *order* before the morning crowd arrives.'

sentences.en: The delivery boxes arrived early and in no sensible *order*: chips on top of bread, cold drinks beside the hot-food shelf, three boxes marked FRAGILE stacked at the very bottom.
I spent an hour sorting everything before the morning rush.
sentences.cn: 我花了一个小时在早上冲刺前把所有东西分类整理。

sentences.en: When the Manager checked at six, she nodded once and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 店长六点来检查的时候，点了一下头，什么都没说。

sentences.en: That nod felt like a gold medal.
sentences.cn: 那个点头的动作感觉像是一枚金牌。

sentences.en: Then she pointed at one box I had missed behind the mop bucket.
sentences.cn: 然后她指了指我漏掉的一个在拖把桶后面的盒子。

event:2.en: Lin from the store across the street appeared just after midnight, holding a flyer. Their shop was running a big *event* on Sunday — free tea samples, a lucky draw, the works. Lin smiled and slid the flyer across my counter without a word. I smiled back and slid it into the recycling. We both understood. When Lin left, I noticed they had actually bought a bottle of water. Even rivals get thirsty.
event:2.cnHint: 午夜后，竞争对手林走进来，悄悄放下了他们店周日活动的传单，介绍了一场特别的____，然后买了瓶水离开。
event:2.hook: Lin paused at the door, glanced back once, then smiled a little too long.
event:2.line: 'Our *event* Sunday will be very popular — just letting you know.'

sentences.en: Lin from the store across the street appeared just after midnight, holding a flyer.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在午夜刚过出现了，手里拿着一张传单。

sentences.en: Their shop was running a big *event* on Sunday — free tea samples, a lucky draw, the works.
Lin smiled and slid the flyer across my counter without a word.
sentences.cn: 林笑了笑，没说话就把传单推过我的柜台。

sentences.en: I smiled back and slid it into the recycling.
sentences.cn: 我也笑了，把它扔进了回收箱。

sentences.en: We both understood.
sentences.cn: 我们都明白。

sentences.en: When Lin left, I noticed they had actually bought a bottle of water.
sentences.cn: 林离开的时候，我注意到他们其实买了一瓶水。

sentences.en: Even rivals get thirsty.
sentences.cn: 再大的对手也会口渴啊。

account:2.en: A regular I had not seen before handed me a store membership card that would not scan. I tried three times. He gave a long *account* of how he had used it just last week, how the Manager herself had set it up, how it had worked perfectly until tonight. His story was detailed and patient. I called the Manager. She had never seen the card before. The man nodded slowly, as if he had expected this answer.
account:2.cnHint: 一位顾客的会员卡扫不出来，他详细____了卡的使用历史，但店长说从没见过这张卡。
account:2.hook: He put the card back in his wallet next to six others that looked exactly the same.
account:2.line: 'Let me give you a full *account* of how I got this card.'

sentences.en: A regular I had not seen before handed me a store membership card that would not scan.
sentences.cn: 一个我没见过的常客递给我一张会员卡，扫不出来。

sentences.en: I tried three times.
sentences.cn: 我试了三次。

sentences.en: He gave a long *account* of how he had used it just last week, how the Manager herself had set it up, how it had worked perfectly until tonight.
His story was detailed and patient.
sentences.cn: 他的故事讲得详细又耐心。

sentences.en: I called the Manager.
sentences.cn: 我给店长打了个电话。

sentences.en: She had never seen the card before.
sentences.cn: 她说从来没见过这张卡。

sentences.en: The man nodded slowly, as if he had expected this answer.
sentences.cn: 那个男人慢慢地点了点头，好像早就猜到了这个答案。

deal:2.en: Tang had made a quiet *deal* with the supplier: buy two boxes of green-tea candy, get one box of fruit candy free. It was a good arrangement, and Tang was proud of it. I found out because all three boxes were hidden behind the instant noodles with a sticky note that said DO NOT SELL — TANG. The Manager found them at the same time I did. They looked at each other for a long, quiet second.
deal:2.cnHint: 唐私下和供应商做了个____，把换来的糖果藏在泡面后面，结果被店长和我同时发现了。
deal:2.hook: Tang's smile did not waver, but both hands gripped the shelf very tight.
deal:2.line: 'It was a fair *deal* — the supplier agreed, I promise.'

sentences.en: Tang had made a quiet *deal* with the supplier: buy two boxes of green-tea candy, get one box of fruit candy free.
It was a good arrangement, and Tang was proud of it.
sentences.cn: 这是个不错的安排，阿糖为此感到骄傲。

sentences.en: I found out because all three boxes were hidden behind the instant noodles with a sticky note that said DO NOT SELL — TANG.
sentences.cn: 我是因为看到三盒糖果都藏在方便面后面，上面贴着一张便签条，写着"禁止出售——阿糖"才发现的。

sentences.en: The Manager found them at the same time I did.
sentences.cn: 店长也在同一时间发现了它们。

sentences.en: They looked at each other for a long, quiet second.
sentences.cn: 他们彼此看了一眼，长长的、安静的一秒钟。

degree:2.en: The old heater behind the counter had one dial with numbers worn off. Tang said to turn it to 'medium,' but without marks that meant nothing. By three in the morning the store had reached a *degree* of warmth that made every customer slow down and linger, like they had all walked into a cosy living room by accident. Even the cat from the alley outside pressed its nose to the glass door. Then the power flickered once.
degree:2.cnHint: 老暖气的刻度盘数字都磨掉了，夜里店里暖到了某种____，让每个顾客都不想走，连巷子里的猫都趴到玻璃门上了。
degree:2.hook: When the lights came back, the cat was somehow inside the store.
degree:2.line: 'The *degree* of warmth in here tonight is really something special.'

sentences.en: The old heater behind the counter had one dial with numbers worn off.
sentences.cn: 柜台后面那个老暖气机上有个表盘，数字都磨掉了。

sentences.en: Tang said to turn it to 'medium,' but without marks that meant nothing.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说转到"中档"，但没有刻度根本没办法操作。

sentences.en: By three in the morning the store had reached a *degree* of warmth that made every customer slow down and linger, like they had all walked into a cosy living room by accident.
Even the cat from the alley outside pressed its nose to the glass door.
sentences.cn: 甚至外面巷子里的那只猫都把鼻子贴在玻璃门上。

sentences.en: Then the power flickered once.
sentences.cn: 然后电灯闪了一下。

traditional:2.en: The Manager taped a hand-written sign above the rice-ball shelf before my shift started. 'We do things the *traditional* way here,' he said, meaning he wrote every price by hand instead of printing labels. The sign was a little crooked, but the customers smiled every time they read it.
traditional:2.cnHint: 店长坚持用手写价签，因为他觉得这才是____的做法。
traditional:2.hook: But one sign at the back of the shelf was not his handwriting.
traditional:2.line: 'We do things the *traditional* way here — handwritten, personal, honest.'

sentences.en: The Manager taped a hand-written sign above the rice-ball shelf before my shift started.
sentences.cn: 店长在我上班前在米团架子上面贴了一张手写的牌子。

sentences.en: 'We do things the *traditional* way here,' he said, meaning he wrote every price by hand instead of printing labels.
The sign was a little crooked, but the customers smiled every time they read it.
sentences.cn: 牌子有点歪，但顾客们每次看到都会笑。

expert:2.en: A quiet woman came in just after two in the morning and stood in front of the instant-noodle wall for a long time. She picked up each cup, read the back, and put it down again. Tang leaned over to me and whispered that she was a food *expert* who tested products for a living. She bought nothing and left a small note on the counter instead.
expert:2.cnHint: 一位深夜光顾的女顾客是食品____，她仔细检查了每一款泡面。
expert:2.hook: The note had a score written on it — and our store got a seven out of ten.
expert:2.line: 'As a food *expert*, I can tell you — three of these noodles are worth buying.'

sentences.en: A quiet woman came in just after two in the morning and stood in front of the instant-noodle wall for a long time.
sentences.cn: 凌晨两点刚过，一个安静的女人走了进来，在泡面墙前站了很久。

sentences.en: She picked up each cup, read the back, and put it down again.
sentences.cn: 她逐个拿起杯子，读背面的字，然后又放回去。

sentences.en: Tang leaned over to me and whispered that she was a food *expert* who tested products for a living.
She bought nothing and left a small note on the counter instead.
sentences.cn: 她什么都没买，只在柜台留下了一张小纸条。

member:2.en: An old man shuffled in and slid a worn card across the counter. It was a loyalty card from before I started working here — nearly full of stamps. 'I am the oldest *member* of this store,' he said proudly, tapping the card twice. I did not know what prize he expected, but his smile suggested he had already decided.
member:2.cnHint: 一位老爷爷拿出快集满的会员卡，自豪地说自己是本店最老的____。
member:2.hook: The back of the card had a phone number written in red ink — the Manager's personal number.
member:2.line: 'I am the oldest *member* of this store, young one — I was here on opening night.'

sentences.en: An old man shuffled in and slid a worn card across the counter.
sentences.cn: 一个老人拖着步子走进来，在柜台上滑过一张破旧的积分卡。

sentences.en: It was a loyalty card from before I started working here — nearly full of stamps.
sentences.cn: 这是我开始在这儿工作之前的积分卡——几乎满满的戳子。

sentences.en: 'I am the oldest *member* of this store,' he said proudly, tapping the card twice.
I did not know what prize he expected, but his smile suggested he had already decided.
sentences.cn: 我不知道他期待什么奖品，但他的笑容暗示他已经有了主意。

heart:2.en: Around three in the morning the street outside went completely silent. Tang set two warm canned drinks on the counter without a word and said, 'The *heart* of a night shift is the quiet hour — you either love it or it breaks you.' I wrapped both hands around the can and decided, right then, that I loved it.
heart:2.cnHint: 阿糖说深夜值班的____就是这段寂静时光，让我第一次感受到了夜班的魅力。
heart:2.hook: Then footsteps — quick, uneven — stopped just outside the glass door.
heart:2.line: 'The *heart* of night shift is this hour — hold onto it.'

sentences.en: Around three in the morning the street outside went completely silent.
sentences.cn: 凌晨三点左右，外面的街道完全安静了下来。

sentences.en: Tang set two warm canned drinks on the counter without a word and said, 'The *heart* of a night shift is the quiet hour — you either love it or it breaks you.'
I wrapped both hands around the can and decided, right then, that I loved it.
sentences.cn: 我用两只手环抱着罐子，就在那一刻决定了，我爱上了这份工作。
